chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Yazid al-Kunasī from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Your son is more entitled to you than your son's son, and your son's son is more entitled to you than your brother, and your full brother (from father and mother) is more entitled to you than your paternal brother, and your paternal brother is more entitled to you than your maternal brother.
He said: And the son of your full brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal brother.
He said: And the son of your paternal brother is more entitled to you than your paternal uncle.
He said: And your paternal uncle who is your father's full brother is more entitled to you than your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother.
He said: And your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother.

He said: And the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's full brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother, and the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's paternal brother is more entitled to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is your father's maternal brother.

key_terms.أَخُوكَ لِأَبِيكَ وَ أُمِّكَ: Your full brother (sharing both father and mother)
key_terms.اِبْنُ عَمِّكَ: Your paternal cousin (son of paternal uncle)

ai.seo_question: What is the order of priority among male relatives in Shia inheritance and kinship law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) details the precise hierarchy of *awlā* (priority in inheritance and guardianship) among male agnatic relatives. It systematically prioritizes full siblings over half-siblings and full cousins over half-cousins, reflecting the juristic principle that closer degrees of kinship through common ancestors hold greater entitlement. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the nuances of *fara'id* (inheritance) and *wilayah* in Shia fiqh.
